deep.reconstruction:
Folio 12v has no mathematical content of its own. It carries only the rectangular library stamp 'NIEDERSÄCHS. STAATS- U. UNIV: BIBLIOTHEK GÖTTINGEN' and mirror-image bleed-through of the ink on the recto (folio 12r, the previous page).

The reversed traces can be matched to the recto text:
- the upper line ending in '...−192∛16 ...' corresponds to '−192∛16 + 200cosφ';
- the middle line reads in mirror as '280 − 192∛16 + 200cosφ';
- the figures lower right read in mirror as '−2.419' and '−1,019'.

The recto computation these traces belong to is as follows. It evaluates f(x) = x^7 − 28x^4 + 280 + 200 cos φ at x = 16^(1/3).
- Since x^3 = 16, x^7 = 256·16^(1/3) and 28x^4 = 448·16^(1/3).
- So f = 280 − 192·16^(1/3) + 200 cos φ.
- The recto then uses logarithms: log10(192) = 2.28330 and log10(16^(1/3)) = 0.40137, summing to 2.68467. So 192·16^(1/3) ≈ 483.8, and 280 − 483.8 ≈ −203.8.
- Dividing by 200 gives ≈ −1.019. The constant part is therefore about −1.019 in units of 200, so f vanishes at this x only if cos φ ≈ 1.019, which is impossible.

The figure −2.419 is presumably an intermediate value, probably 1.4 − 3.819 or similar; this is uncertain. Nothing new is derived on 12v itself.
errors: No errors on 12v itself (no original content).
